articles.headline: NFL survivor power rankings: Why this is the week to use the Bills or the Texans
articles.description: ESPN NFL survivor pool strategy, predictions and ranking the top six options for Week 11.
articles.headlineJa: NFLサバイバー・パワーランキング：今週ビルズかテキサンズを起用すべき理由
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNによるNFLサバイバープールの戦略、予想、および第11週のトップ6オプションのランキング。
articles.body:
Each of the first eight weeks saw an underdog of a touchdown or more pull off the upset, but since then, the last two weeks have been dominated by favorites. Closing line favorites of at least four points are 16-1 outright over the last two weeks, with the only loss coming by the Houston Texans last week against the Cleveland Browns.

Week 11 is shaping up to be another great week for favorites. As of Wednesday morning, the average point spread is 8.1, which would be the highest prior to the final two weeks of the season since 1987.

Five teams are double-digit favorites, including the two biggest favorites all season -- the Buffalo Bills and the Kansas City Chiefs. There are also two more favorites of at least a touchdown, and the 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers are also laying more than a field goal.

With so many strong options, the biggest decisions involve looking at selection rate, future value and your path to Week 18. Every one of the double-digit favorites has multiple additional weeks where they will likely be similar-sized favorites down the road.

Out of the five double-digit favorites, the one with the least future value is the Chicago Bears. However, they are currently tracking to be the most-selected team on ESPN.

The Bills will likely be the chalk pick in most contests, though not on ESPN, where they are 30% available. The Chiefs are the other massive favorite, but they are 13% available on ESPN, and even lower in some other contests. If you somehow have them available, they are a fine pick, but you can also save them for later when they will be even less owned with potentially fewer other elite options.

The Texans are the third-biggest favorites according to the betting market, but with so many other options, the 3-6 team playing on Thursday could slip through the cracks and be a great contrarian pick.

The Denver Broncos are the last double-digit favorite, and they are also widely available. They have five future weeks with at least a 75% chance to win, blending models from ESPN Analytics and Mike Clay, tied for most of any team. This could be one of the last times to get them as a big favorite at relatively light selection, but you are giving up immediate win equity and the chance to use them down the road.

As for the rest of the board, the Dallas Cowboys are the only other team that combines strong win probability with lack of future value, especially if you can cover next week when they host the Philadelphia Eagles. However, Dallas is currently 21% selected, so you aren't getting an edge there at all.

In double-pick pools, the Carolina Panthers, Pittsburgh Steelers and Chargers are strong plays with Carolina being the preferred option if available.

articles.headline: Updated NBA championship and MVP odds: Heat on the rise, Wemby ahead of Luka
articles.description: The Heat have bounced back from a rough start to the season, while Victor Wembanyama is now the leader for MVP just ahead of Luka Doncic.
articles.headlineJa: NBA優勝およびMVPオッズ更新：ヒートが上昇、ウェンビーがルカを上回る
articles.descriptionJa: ヒートはシーズン序盤の不調から立ち直り、ヴィクター・ウェンバンヤマがルカ・ドンチッチを僅差で抑えてMVPの筆頭候補となった。
articles.body:
The beginning of the Giannis Antetokounmpo era for the Miami Heat hasn't gone exactly according to plan, but the team is starting to heat up as it heads into its highly anticipated first matchup with the Milwaukee Bucks. Miami began the season with 11th-best NBA Finals odds at 30-1 and lengthened out to 55-1 early in the season, but amid a run of five straight wins, the Heat are back down to 40-1 for this season's title.

The San Antonio Spurs remain the championship favorites at +300, with the Oklahoma City Thunder continuing to lose ground, going from +450 to +500 week-over-week. The Boston Celtics (+750), Philadelphia 76ers (+800) and reigning champion New York Knicks (10-1) round out the top five.

Meanwhile, MVP is becoming a true two-man race between the Spurs' Victor Wembanyama and the Los Angeles Lakers' Luka Doncic. The former took over the lead in the past week, moving from +165 to +120, while the latter also shortened but not enough to maintain the lead, going from +145 to +135.

Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.

articles.headline: Miami Heat players receive GTA VI care packages from Rockstar Games
articles.description: Heat players received a custom game-themed care package complete with custom controllers, consoles and, of course, a copy of the game.
articles.headlineJa: マイアミ・ヒートの選手たちがロックスター・ゲームスから『GTA VI』のケアパッケージを受け取る
articles.descriptionJa: ヒートの選手たちは、特製コントローラーやゲーム機、そしてもちろんゲームソフト本体が含まれた、ゲームをテーマにした特製ギフトセットを受け取った。
articles.body:
Players around the NBA are gearing up for "Grand Theft Auto VI," but some are going to be particularly ready for the game's highly anticipated Thursday release: Miami Heat players.

The ties between Miami and the Grand Theft Auto series date back to 2002 with "Grand Theft Auto: Vice City." The fourth game in the series, it is set in a fictional city based on Miami. GTA VI returns to Vice City.

Unsurprisingly for a team that has been meticulously embracing Vice City branding for years, the Heat are rolling out an impressive promotion ahead of GTA VI going live Thursday. Wednesday will be "A Night in Vice City" at the Kaseya Center, featuring a new court design, concessions and more.

But the promotional street runs both ways -- and Miami players are reaping the benefits.

A number of players, including Davion Mitchell, Nick Richards, Tim Hardaway Jr. and more posted about receiving a game-themed care package from Rockstar Games, PlayStation and luggage company Rimowa for GTA VI's release. It included custom controllers, consoles and, of course, a copy of the game. The care package came in a fitting color scheme -- Miami's Vice City pink and black alternate branding.

Mitchell, who posted about the gift on his Instagram story, added a humorous caption:

"I'm about to deactivate my account because I'm about to lock in," he wrote, adding saluting and laughing emojis. "It's up!!!"

The Heat will face the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night (7 p.m. EST, ESPN).

articles.headline: Stroud: Texans' home skid and 17-point collapse fuel 'scary' urgency vs Colts
articles.description: — C.J. Stroud certainly isn’t thrilled with where his Houston Texans are entering Thursday night’s AFC South matchup with Indianapolis.
articles.headlineJa: ストラウド：テキサンズのホーム連敗と17点差の逆転負けが、コルツ戦への「恐ろしいほどの」切迫感に拍車
articles.descriptionJa: C.J.ストラウドは、木曜夜に行われるインディアナポリスとのAFCサウス対決を前に、ヒューストン・テキサンズの現状に決して満足していない。
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- — C.J. Stroud certainly isn’t thrilled with where his Houston Texans are entering Thursday night’s AFC South matchup with Indianapolis.


              But the quarterback believes that he and the Texans respond well when their backs are against the wall.


              “I’m not the happiest camper, but I think the motivated me is one of the best me’s that I’ve seen,” he said. “I think even as (a) team, the motivated Texans is a scary team. It’s up to us. We don’t need anybody else.”


              The Texans will try and get back on track after squandering a 17-point lead in a 27-24 loss at Cleveland on Sunday dropped them to 3-6. They’ll meet a Colts team in a similar place at 3-7, but that snapped a five-game skid with a victory over the Dolphins last week. 


              “I think it’s big to get a win,” Colts coach Shane Steichen said. “It’s been five weeks and obviously we get one and so you get a little bit of momentum. Guys are feeling good ... so, it’s awesome to get that win, but we’ve got another challenge coming up.”


              Steichen knows the key to success against the Texans will be to limit Stroud and he raved about his performance this season.


              “He’s making a lot of big-time throws,” he said. “The ball’s coming out of his hands. Guys are separating and even when it’s tight coverage, the ball placement, the accuracy has been pinpoint.”


              The Colts got a 19-17 win in the first meeting with Houston this season and a victory on Thursday will give them their first season sweep of the Texans since 2021 and leave them in second place in the division behind Jacksonville.


              “Anytime you go against a division opponent, it means a little bit more,” Steichen said. “So, we’re excited for that challenge and that opportunity coming up on Thursday.”


              Houston’s entire season has been disappointing, but perhaps the most disheartening is the team’s performance at home. The Texans are 0-4 at Reliant Stadium, capped by a 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants on Oct. 25.


              After entering the season with Super Bowl aspirations, the Texans are now scrambling to try and hold onto their dwindling hopes of reaching the playoffs.


              “It doesn’t feel good. It’s frustrating,” defensive end Will Anderson said. “Obviously, we’re not in a position that we want to be in, but we’re not going to waver. We’re not going to change anything for anybody. We’re going to continue to play our brand of ball.”


              Need to know
              Indianapolis (3-7) at Houston (3-6).


              When/where to watch: Thursday, 8:15 p.m. EST, Prime Video.


              Latest odds: Texans by 12 ½.


              Against the spread: Colts 5-5; Texans 3-6.


              Last week: Colts beat Dolphins 24-22; Texans lost to Browns 27-24.


              Last meeting: Colts beat Texans 19-17 on Sept. 27 in Indianapolis.

articles.headline: Sources: Brandon Aiyuk contacted Jayden Daniels to mend friendship with star QB
articles.description: Brandon Aiyuk and Jayden Daniels have patched up their relationship after a falling out earlier this year, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：ブランドン・アイユクがスターQBジェイデン・ダニエルズに連絡し、友情の修復を試みた
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNが伝えた関係者によると、ブランドン・アイユクとジェイデン・ダニエルズは、今年初めに不仲となった関係を修復したという。
articles.body:
Brandon Aiyuk and Jayden Daniels have patched up their relationship after a falling out earlier this year, sources told ESPN.

Aiyuk, who was reinstated last week and is attempting to determine his NFL future, reached out to Daniels about a month ago to reconcile with the Washington Commanders star quarterback, according to sources.

The former college teammates' relationship was strained over the summer when Aiyuk criticized Daniels and his mother, Regina Jackson, as part of a series of social media posts.

But sources told ESPN that after talking things out, Daniels was receptive and understanding of Aiyuk.

The NFL reinstated Aiyuk on Nov. 9 after the wide receiver reported for a physical with the San Francisco 49ers, who received a two-game roster exemption to sort through any remaining business with the seven-year veteran. That exemption expires next Monday after San Francisco's Week 11 game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City.

Aiyuk took to social media multiple times over the summer to voice his displeasure with the Niners and attempted to goad them into releasing him while also saying he wouldn't "do business" with the team at all. On multiple occasions, he also implied or openly suggested that he wanted to join the Commanders to play with Daniels, with whom he had formed a friendship in their time together at Arizona State.

That friendship was strained by Aiyuk's subsequent social media posts aimed at Daniels, but the pair have since settled those differences. It is unclear whether the recent conversation will have any bearing over Aiyuk potentially joining Daniels and the Commanders.

Aiyuk, 28, has been on the Niners' reserve/left squad list since December, but he took steps toward reinstatement in recent weeks, hiring agent Drew Rosenhaus and filing the reinstatement paperwork in late October.

Aiyuk has not played since tearing the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee on Oct. 20, 2024. The Niners have until Monday to place Aiyuk on their 53-man roster or release him.

articles.headline: How fallen giants and their fans bounce back from scandal, relegation
articles.description: Some of Europe's greatest teams have suffered relegation as punishment. So what might lie ahead for Man City?
articles.headlineJa: 没落した名門クラブとファンは、いかにしてスキャンダルや降格から立ち直るのか
articles.descriptionJa: 欧州の偉大なチームの中には、罰則として降格を経験したチームもある。マンチェスター・シティには何が待ち受けているのだろうか。
articles.body:
What does it feel like to realize the club you love is stuck in a doom spiral of its own making?

Whether due to cheating, financial mismanagement or general ineptitude, some of Europe's greatest teams have suffered the ignominy of relegation by means of punishment -- and their supporters have watched it unfold. From Juventus and Fiorentina in Italy to Rangers in Scotland, fans have seen offices stripped bare and managers and players scrambling for places on the first boats off the sinking ship.

But a crisis offers the chance for heroes to drag their team out of the deep while suits swap seats in the boardrooms. And amid schadenfreude, anger and denial, supporters of flawed giants find unity through their morbid, self-deprecating humor and fortitude in their situation.

As Manchester City's fans await the results of their appeal and the level of punishment for their 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules, they might find some small comfort in seeing how others have bounced back from the depths of despair ... or renewed dread at the tribulations that could lie ahead.

Fleeing for greener pastures

By the time manager Fabio Capello had sprinted to Real Madrid in 2006, taking stars Emerson and Fabio Cannavaro with him, Juventus' offices had already been ransacked.

The "Calciopoli" scandal started as a doping investigation into Juventus, but instead found evidence of attempted match-fixing by executives who manipulated referees and their bosses -- a scandal that also implicated Fiorentina, AC Milan, Reggina and Lazio. Papers, contracts and hard drives were seized by the Guardia di Finanza (Financial Police) on May 18, 2006.

The original swath of punishments was handed out just six days after Italy won the 2006 World Cup. Juventus were hammered the hardest; they were kicked down to Serie B and stripped of their 2005 and 2006 league titles, triggering a flurry of expedited exit strategies.

"This world had been turned upside down," Ibrahimovic wrote in his 2011 autobiography. "It wasn't possible to take it all in. We'd won two titles in a row -- were we going to lose everything? One after one the players got away ... every one of us who were left called our agents: 'Sell us, sell us.'

"Uncertainty and desperation hung in the air ... No way was I going to sacrifice a year in the second division. My best years were in danger of being wasted; I told [agent Mino Raiola], 'Do whatever it takes, just get me out of here.'"

Ibrahimovic watched teammates Lilian Thuram and Gianluca Zambrotta join Barcelona, while Patrick Vieira headed to Internazionale. Didier Deschamps took charge, though he couldn't persuade Ibrahimovic to stay. Ibrahimovic said he'd train but wouldn't play in matches, leading to the striker refusing to get on the bus for a preseason game -- instead, he hid in his room and played video games, eventually joining Vieira at Inter.

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino arrives at Man United: 'You will see, give me time'
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United for his first day as head coach on Wednesday but said he requires "time" to turn the club's fortunes around.
articles.headlineJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノがマン・ユナイテッドに就任：「見ていてくれ、時間をくれ」
articles.descriptionJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノは水曜日、ヘッドコーチとしての初日でマンチェスター・ユナイテッドに到着したが、クラブの運命を変えるには「時間」が必要だと語った。
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United for his first day as head coach on Wednesday but said he requires "time" to turn the club's fortunes around.

Pochettino's final act in charge of the United States national side was a 2-0 victory over Haiti in Cincinnati on Tuesday night.

A plane carrying Pochettino arrived at Manchester Airport on Wednesday afternoon. He headed to the club's training ground, Carrington, as the replacement for the sacked Michael Carrick before his first game leading United on Sunday against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League.

On Tuesday night, Pochettino was told by former Manchester City and United States player DaMarcus Beasley that "Manchester is blue, it will always be blue."

He responded: "You will see. Give me time.

"The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it's adrenalin you want to feel. We need to add our common sense... we know the situation is not a situation that deserves to be a club like Manchester United, the fan base is amazing."

Pochettino added: "The mentality is to learn from everyone. You need to have an open mind because I think the players can teach us every day, we are much better coaching staff now.

"Football is about attitude, and it's about the approach. It's about connection, feelings and communication."

Upon arrival at Carrington, Pochettino said he is "very excited to be here. It's an honour. It's a privilege to be in this amazing club. Yes, looking forward to start to work."

United have confirmed Jesus Perez, Miguel D'Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino as Pochettino's staff. 

Mauricio Pochettino starts work at Man United on Wednesday

Pochettino was also asked about whether he can improve United's running statistics, which were criticised by ex-boss Carrick after a drab 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League.

In response to Bruno Fernandes' questioning of the team's tactics, Carrick said: "Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

Pochettino said on Tuesday night: "What I can talk in general, football is very complex and I think it's not important if you run or not run.

"You need to run well, you need to run with an objective, you need to run together. Then you need to play, you need to know what you need to do, you need to express your talent. The mindsets are so important."

Pochettino led the U.S. to the round of 16 at last summer's World Cup on home soil.

But he is now returning to the Premier League where he has previously coached Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool, Bayern battle for Gladbach teen Wael Mohya
articles.description: Liverpool and Bayern Munich are interested in Borussia Mönchengladbach attacking midfielder Wael Mohya. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Borussia Mönchengladbach attacking midfielder Wael Mohya is on the radar of Liverpool and Bayern Munich, while Manchester United defender Matthijs de Ligt could leave the club for Besiktas. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool and Bayern Munich are interested in Borussia Mönchengladbach attacking midfielder Wael Mohya, Bild reports. The 17-year-old has been scouted "intensively" by clubs in Europe, following impressive performances from the No. 10 position which recently earned him a call up to the senior Germany team from manager Jürgen Klopp. He has scored two goals and provided one assist in nine Bundesliga matches this season, and has also been linked with Brighton, Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig.

- Manchester United defender Matthijs de Ligt is on the radar of Besiktas, TEAMtalk reports. The Turkish Süper Lig club are exploring a January move for the 27-year-old, and the Red Devils could consider parting ways with him amid plans to refresh their defensive options, though any loan deal would require an obligation to be made permanent. Fulham's Calvin Bassey, 26, has recently been linked as a potential replacement.

- Arsenal, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain are keen on AFC Bournemouth forward Junior Kroupi, according to The Sun. The Gunners are long-term admirers of the 20-year-old, who has been in impressive form since returning from injury in October and scored in France's 2-1 Nations League win over Turkey on Nov. 15. The Premier League champions are among multiple teams tracking Kroupi, but there could be hesitancy to make an approach in January due to the fact his transfer is expected to require an offer worth £100 million.

- Meanwhile, Bournemouth are also set to demand an offer of £100 million before agreeing to part ways with midfielder Alex Scott, amid interest from Liverpool, Arsenal, and Chelsea, the Daily Star reports. All three clubs are pursuing a move for the 23-year-old in January, but the Cherries are determined to keep hold of him despite Scott turning down multiple contract extension offers. Scott hasn't featured since picking up a thigh injury during England's 7-0 Nations League victory over Croatia on Oct. 3.

- Bayern Munich have made contact regarding a move for Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha, according to TEAMtalk. The Bundesliga side are said to have registered fresh interest with the 18-year-old's representatives, but the Reds have no plans to listen to offers, and see him as a player that could become one of the top players in Europe. Ngumoha is set to enter the final 18 months of his deal at Anfield in January.

articles.headline: As Nike replaces Adidas, is UEFA Champions League star ball on its way out?
articles.description: Nike will replace Adidas as supplier of UEFA Champions League match balls from next season. Will the famous 'star ball' design soon be no more?
articles.body:
Editor's note: This article was first published on Aug. 26, 2026 and has been updated 

The UEFA Champions League and UEFA Women's Champions League match balls will boast a brand new look starting next season after UEFA confirmed on Monday that Nike will be taking over from long-standing provider Adidas as the official supplier for the 2027-28 campaign onwards.

Nike will take the reins for the 2027-28 campaign onward after agreeing a deal to supply the official match balls for all three UEFA club competitions from 2027 to 2031 -- the Champions League, the Europa League and the Conference League. According to The Guardian, that deal is worth around $45 million a year, double the value of the final contract with Adidas.

- Champions League talking points: Are Como the real deal?

With Adidas having supplied the official Champions League match ball since 2001, the "star ball" design has become an emblem of the competition. However, the last we see of the iconic pattern might be in the 2026-27 final.

That's because, as things stand, there are no specific details available as to the designs that Nike has in store. In a statement on Monday, UEFA would only say: "Further details on the match ball designs will be revealed in due course." It is also unclear -- and highly unlikely -- that the American sportswear giant will continue with the star theme popularised by Adidas over the past 25 years, as the German powerhouse reportedly hold the rights to the star ball design.

Nike's designs are therefore likely to be fresh and distinct with the intent of drawing a line under Adidas' tenure as UEFA match ball suppliers while also launching their own, modernised visual identity.

Back in August, Adidas unveiled what will be their final iteration of the "star ball," the preliminary eye-catching colourway of which is currently being used throughout the group phase of the 2026-27 Champions League.

The men's version of the 2026-27 Champions League ball is plastered in a neon-spattered livery that, according to Adidas, has been inspired by players creating colourful moments of magic and personal expression while plugging away at training on cold, foggy training pitches during their quest to attain Champions League greatness.

The design for the women's match ball is a little less abstract. The golden-orange pattern takes its inspiration from the aura of the ring of 11 stars that make up the UWCL emblem, with flashes of metallic purple and silver then adding a dash of visual contrast to the mix.

Both balls are based on the template that Adidas have used for their Champions League match balls since the introduction of the "Finale 1" ball for the 2001-02 season.
